samples.summary: The v1 PUT re-implements the shared numeric band instead of calling the module this same change created for it. `bandSlideBlockNumerics` (1114) and `bandSlideCellNumerics` (1147) are a near-verbatim copy of `bandOneBlock` in `packages/docs/src/model/numeric-attrs.ts` (336-413) — same fields (`style.lineHeight`, `listLevel`, `tableData.rowHeights`, `columnWidths` sliced at `MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS`, cell `padding`, `colSpan`/`rowSpan`), same drop-vs-clamp rules, even the same comments. Likewise `assertValidTableData`'s new `columnWidths` cap (965) is a verbatim copy of `bandTableColumnWidths` in `packages/slides/src/model/band-numerics.ts`, duplicated again in both packages' tests. The backend already imports `@wafflebase/docs` (it pulls `MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS` and every `normalize*` from it) and `@wafflebase/slides` (`slides.controller.ts`), so `bandBlockNumerics` / `bandElementNumerics` were available as a call. This is exactly the divergence the repo's own comments warn about (`serialize/markdown.ts`: "a rule enforced by two copies drifts"), and the design doc this change writes asserts the opposite of what it shipped: docs/design/docs/docs.md now says the walk "lives in one place … and each reader calls it, rather than each reader being a fresh chance to forget." With two copies, the next band added to `numeric-attrs.ts` silently does not apply to anything stored through `PUT /content`.
samples.evidence: backend bandSlideBlockNumerics (1114-1164) vs docs bandOneBlock (numeric-attrs.ts:336-413); backend assertValidTableData columnWidths (965) vs slides bandTableColumnWidths

samples.summary: Master placeholder typography is now banded by two implementations that give different answers for the same input. `bandMasterPlaceholderStyles` (backend, 610) *deletes* a `fontSize`/`lineHeight` that normalizes to `undefined` and *400s* a non-number, while `bandPlaceholderStyleNumerics` (`packages/slides/src/model/band-numerics.ts`) substitutes `DEFAULT_MASTER`'s value for the same input and never rejects — its own JSDoc argues these are required numbers so `undefined` "would paint NaNpx". So the write path can store a master slot the read path considers impossible, and a deck whose master a peer wrote with a string `fontSize` is echoed by `GET` and then rejected by `PUT`, breaking the GET → edit → PUT round-trip the controller's own comment says must keep working. One rule, two implementations, already divergent on both branches.
samples.evidence: backend bandMasterPlaceholderStyles throws BadRequestException for non-number and `delete style[field]` when banded === undefined; slides bandPlaceholderStyleNumerics uses `?? fallback.fontSize`

samples.summary: The canonical REST design doc still describes the old `PUT` contract. It states `masters[]` "needs no walk — a `Master` is `{ id, themeId, background, placeholderStyles }` and holds no elements and no `Block`s" (356-358), which this change deliberately reverses (the controller now walks `masters[].placeholderStyles` and 400s a wrong-typed `fontSize`). It also documents only `MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH` for the element walk (430) with no mention of the new block-walk depth cap, and its "`PUT` validation contract" section (334-428) frames repairs as "empty shape" fill-ins only — it does not record the new class of behaviour this change adds, namely numeric *value* repair (clamping `fontSize`/`lineHeight`/`padding`/spans/`columnWidths`, dropping out-of-band inline images) on write. The docs-side doc (docs/design/docs/docs.md) was updated but rest-api.md, the doc that owns this endpoint's contract, was not.

`sanitizeDocStyles` changes the trust model and the read/write shape of the named-style registry (`stylesJson`) — it now bands `fontSize`/`lineHeight`, drops non-finite offsets, strips any `image`, and reduces `inlineDark` to colour-only, and the sanitized object is what gets written back — but no design doc records it. docs/design/docs/docs-named-styles.md is the canonical doc for the registry and is untouched; the new docs.md section covers block/attribute bands and never mentions `stylesJson`. Grepping docs/design for `stylesJson`/`sanitizeDocStyles` returns nothing at all, so a reader of the registry's design cannot learn that a stored entry is now rewritten on load.

Scope past a decision the task plan recorded twice. `docs/tasks/active/20260908-docs-list-level-subtree-todo.md` lists the DOCX importer as an unaudited producer and says "Auditing and bounding an importer is its own change" (round 10), repeated as still-deferred in round 11 — yet this branch bands `w:sz` and `w:line` in `docx-style-map.ts` with new tests. Round 10 also states "the numeric-hardening program is not extended to any new attribute", while this branch extends it to master placeholder typography, layout placeholder specs, the board store, revision snapshots and `deckFontScale`/`pxPerPt`. None of that new scope is recorded in the todo or the paired lessons file (no round-12 section exists), so the plan of record no longer describes the change.
samples.evidence: todo.md:165-172 'Auditing and bounding an importer is its own change'; todo.md:136 'the numeric-hardening program is not extended to any new attribute'

samples.summary: The same depth ceiling of 32 now exists as three independent constants — `MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH` (backend controller), `MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH` (docs `numeric-attrs.ts`) and `MAX_GROUP_DEPTH` (slides `band-numerics.ts`) — and the band ceilings themselves are split across three modules (`list-level.ts`, `row-height.ts`, `numeric-attrs.ts`) whose split is historical rather than conceptual. The copies are justified in comments (dependency direction slides → docs), and the task file already lists "restructuring the band modules" as deferred, so this is a note rather than a defect.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. `bandSlideBlockNumerics` (docs-content.controller.ts:1114-1144) and `bandSlideCellNumerics` (:1147-1164) reproduce, field for field and in places comment for comment, `bandOneBlock` in packages/docs/src/model/numeric-attrs.ts:336-413 — same lineHeight/listLevel/rowHeights handling, same `.slice(0, MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS).map(normalizeColumnRatio(...) ?? 0)` column rule, same cell padding and colSpan/rowSpan drop-vs-clamp policy including the identical `expandCellRangeForMerges` comment. `assertValidTableData`'s new cap (:965-967) is the same expression as `bandTableColumnWidths` in packages/slides/src/model/band-numerics.ts:72-77, with a near-identical rationale comment. Reuse was concretely available: `bandBlockNumerics` is exported at packages/docs/src/index.ts:112 and node.ts:155, `bandElementNumerics`/`bandSlidesDocumentNumerics` at packages/slides/src/index.ts:61,65, and the controller already imports from `@wafflebase/docs` (:44-58) while the backend already depends on `@wafflebase/slides` (slides.controller.ts). The design doc this change touches asserts the opposite discipline at docs/design/docs/docs.md:286-290 ("the walk lives in one place … each reader calls it"). No refutation ground fits: the code is present as described, nothing makes it unreachable, and duplication/reuse is explicitly in the design-fit lane. Severity stands at major under the rubric's "duplicated logic that will now diverge and give two answers to the same question": a band added to numeric-attrs.ts will not reach content stored through PUT /content. The one nuance (the scalar normalizers themselves are shared; only the walk wiring and field policy are copied) softens but does not remove the divergence risk.

verdict.reason: Both implementations exist exactly as described and diverge on both branches. Backend `bandMasterPlaceholderStyles` (docs-content.controller.ts:610-636) throws BadRequestException for a present non-number (623-627) and `delete style[field]` when the normalizer returns undefined (632). Slides `bandPlaceholderStyleNumerics` (packages/slides/src/model/band-numerics.ts:180-200) runs the same docs normalizers but substitutes `?? fallback.fontSize` / `?? fallback.lineHeight` from DEFAULT_MASTER (194-198) and never rejects (non-numbers are coerced away by asFiniteNumber, 49-51); its JSDoc (150-156) explicitly states these are required numbers so an undefined would paint NaNpx — i.e. the two copies disagree about whether the backend's delete branch is even a legal state. Reuse was concretely available: bandPlaceholderStyleNumerics/bandMasterNumerics are exported from packages/slides/src/node.ts:60-65, backend depends on @wafflebase/slides (packages/backend/package.json:48) and already imports it (src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:21, src/yorkie/slide-ops.ts:1). The round-trip consequence is also supported: readSlidesRoot returns masters verbatim with no band (slides-tree.ts:65), so a peer-written string fontSize is echoed by GET and 400ed by PUT, contradicting the round-trip invariant the controller itself repeatedly states (docs-content.controller.ts:1311, 370, 383, 777, 1054, 1257). The only partial defense — that an API boundary rejects while a reader repairs (stated at 1265-1266) — explains the non-number branch but not the drop-vs-default divergence, so it does not refute the duplication. Duplicated logic that already gives two answers to the same question is the design-fit rubric's named major case.
